chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the crescent of Ramadan when it is uncertain to us on the twenty-ninth of Sha'ban - so he said: 'Do not fast it unless you see it. And if the people of another town testify that they have seen it, then complete the fast. And if you see it in the middle of the day, then complete its fast until the night.'
He means by his saying (peace be upon him) 'complete its fast until the night' on the condition that it is from Sha'ban, without intending that it is from Ramadan.

key_terms.شَهَادَ أَهْلُ بَلَدٍ آخَرَ: Testimony of the people of another town
key_terms.وَسَطَ النَّهَارِ: In the middle of the day

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the Ramadan crescent is seen during the day on the 29th of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential stance on lunar sighting (*ru'yah*), emphasizing that local sighting is primary but allows for following another community's testimony to conclude the month. It specifically addresses the scenario of seeing the crescent mid-day, ruling that the fast counts as voluntary Sha'ban unless one explicitly intends it as Ramadan, highlighting the importance of *niyyah* (intention) in distinguishing between obligatory and voluntary acts. This reflects the Shia reliance on actual visual confirmation rather than astronomical calculation alone, a key distinction from some Sunni schools.
